findings.description: Returned invalid UTF-8 extraction formerly shared decode_error with pre-extraction entity decoding. Removing every extraction_* field and parser from that rejected receipt could bypass retention verification. Distinct extraction_decode_error now requires extraction metadata; original deletion probe is rejected while real invalid HTML entity decoding remains a legitimate failed receipt.

Current runtime cache key and owner include policy; required policy is checked for fresh and cached receipts. Old cache/history remains but cannot become a current-policy cache hit. Legacy audit explicitly reports not_recorded_by_legacy_policy.

Rejected bytes, length, SHA, decoded character count, complete forbidden-control distribution and failure reason are checked. Failed downloads with durable receipt IDs cannot lose telemetry, and receipt identity is bound to request/owner.

limits: Policy detects forbidden Unicode Cc controls and invalid UTF-8; it does not certify semantic correctness, visual glyph fidelity, or general document readability.

New full-rejected-extraction retention covers bytes returned by extraction before validation. Existing nonzero Poppler exit remains pdf_extraction_error with raw PDF and stderr reason; it does not promise stdout retention.
Receipt integrity checks artifact/metadata agreement and current consumer policy. A fully coordinated rewrite of all archive evidence requires an external archive hash authority to detect.
Legacy archives retain transport integrity checks but do not retroactively earn the new readability validation.
No change to network retry/fallback, model, budget or process-cleanup policy was introduced by the reviewed diff.
